target: The designer's sections D to H: in-company customs classification as the wedge, "feature inside an existing workflow product" as the competitive-threat call, the 10-interview discovery sprint, and the 300 to 500 case base-rate experiment with its six gates. Evidence limitation: this review had no WebSearch and could reach only GitHub hosts. I re-fetched and recomputed the CROSS scrape (216,164 rows) and the Avalara and HMRC source files the design cites; every other number below is from the digest and cluster files, or is labelled estimate or recall. Nothing here measures category H anywhere.

refuted.point: Gate 3 (capture failure: at least 50% of category 7 cases show the prior settlement was re-decided or contradicted rather than applied).
refuted.why: The design's own category definition makes this gate vacuous. Category 7 is defined as cases where a prior settlement existed and 'a human nonetheless re-decided it, or decided inconsistently with it'; a case where the prior settlement was found and applied is coded 1 with the class key retained. So by construction 100% of category 7 cases are re-decided or contradicted and gate 3 always passes. The quantity the gate wants is the re-decision rate among all cases where a prior settlement existed: 7 divided by (7 plus 1-with-class-key). That ratio must be named as the gate and the 1-with-class-key count must be reported.

refuted.point: Gate 2 (recurrence: at least 50% of category 7 plus 8 decisions fall in classes with three or more occurrences in the window, 'counting unsampled items in the same class').
refuted.why: The class key for 7 and 8 is '6-digit line or product family, times the interpretive question type'. The question type is known only for coded cases; unsampled items in the window carry a code and a family but no interpretive question, so they cannot be assigned to a class without coding them all. As written the recurrence count is either uncomputable or silently collapses to line-or-family recurrence, which counts factual repeats (every garment in 6110) as interpretive recurrence, the exact conflation the customs verifier warned against (digest, tax-customs cluster, verifier 'manual review conflated' item 1). A 12-month window also censors recurrence: settlements made late in the window cannot recur.

refuted.point: Coder B: 'a trained analyst without customs background, working from the codebook and ten worked examples, so that the codebook, not domain intuition, carries the categories'.
refuted.why: The decision tree cannot be executed without tariff competence. Q2 asks whether the coder could reproduce the code in under five minutes from the schedule notes and a family template; Q3 asks whether essential character or principal function was determined under a rule whose meaning was not in dispute; Q4 asks whether the decision turned on what a rule text means. A non-specialist cannot answer any of these, so a kappa failure at the pilot gate would not show that facts and interpretation are inseparable in the records (the finding the design says it would report); it would show that one coder could not read the tariff. The prior IPSA kappa of 0.78 to 1.0 (prior_evidence.md, hash-verified PDFs) was on published, reasoned review documents, not on item-master rows, and does not transfer. Both coders need domain competence with independent affiliations; the codebook's carrying power should be tested by a third, non-specialist pass on a subsample, not by making the non-specialist a gate coder.

refuted.point: Gate 5 (public duplication: fewer than 50% of category 7 plus 8 settlements match a public ruling on the same 10-digit line and question at the decision date; otherwise pivot to retrieval).
refuted.why: Two defects. First, the CROSSFetch CSV the design names as the lookup source has only these columns: id, rulingNumber, subject, categories, rulingDate, isUsmca, isNafta, collection, relatedRulings, modifiedBy, modifies, revokedBy, revokes, tariffs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justinmoonjeli/CROSSFetch/main/cbp_rulings_data.csv, open-source scrape, fetched and parsed this session). It carries no ruling text, so 'same question' cannot be checked from it; a full-text corpus would be needed. Second, at line level the match is near-universal by construction: 89.1% of 2023-24 CBP rulings already sit on a 10-digit line with a prior ruling and 99.0% on a 6-digit line (my recomputation of the same CSV, matching the design's figures). A US importer's decisions will match a prior ruling on the same line for almost every case, so the gate as specified fails by construction and forces the pivot regardless of what the company log shows.

refuted.point: 'Brokers hold classification worksheets for many importers at once, so one broker relationship yields several logs.'
refuted.why: Broker classification records are the importer's confidential business records; [RECALL, unverified] US broker regulations (19 CFR 111.24) bar disclosure of client records to third parties without client consent. Each importer log obtained through a broker therefore needs that importer's separate consent and NDA, so the broker route does not multiply logs at low cost; it multiplies consent negotiations. The broker also earns per-line classification fees (design's own recall), so a broker partner has a direct interest in the experiment not finding removable labour. Neither point appears in the sequencing plan, which puts the two brokers first and relies on their referrals.

weakened.point: Gate 1: categories 7 plus 8 at least 15% of the escalation stratum, presented as derived from customer economics.
weakened.why: The design's own model gives required h = 3P / (r N C) = 36% at its central estimates (N = 2,500, C = $200, r = 0.5, P = $30,000; all estimates, no sourced figure). The 15% figure comes from the tail scenario L of at least $1.2M (5,000 escalations at $240), both parameters above central. The design does say the interview-supplied L overrides, but it then fixes 15% as the written gate, which is the number a reader will carry. This is the pattern the brief warns against: the headline gate is the one the project can pass, the central-economics gate (36%) is above every H estimate in the project (5 to 15%, customs verifier). The gate should be written as a formula with the interview values filled in before coding, with 36% stated as the central-case value, and the 15% cited only as the payments verifier's kill line (digest, payments cluster: 'class-level H must exceed roughly 15-20% of escalations at thousands per year'). Separately, r = 0.5 is applied to category 8 in year one; a newly settled ambiguity saves nothing at its first occurrence, only on reuse, so year-one S should count h7 at r and h8 at the expected within-year reuse rate, and the capture cost (one hour per settlement, design's estimate) should be subtracted.

weakened.point: Coding order Q1 first (missing fact causing a request, hold or delay implies primary 2) with thresholds applied to the primary code only.
weakened.why: The rule order sends every case that had both a facts request and an interpretive question to category 2. The prior IPSA study found 16 to 20 of 46 outcomes relied on facts gathered after the original decision while rule meaning was the primary issue in 12 (prior_evidence.md), so co-occurrence is common. Applying the gates to primary only makes the H share a floor set by a convention. Report the primary-or-secondary H share alongside, and pre-register which one the gate uses.

weakened.point: Gate 6 and the packet's 'which HMRC Decision elements the record holds' protect against thin records.
weakened.why: They do not. The decision tree always yields a code: in a company whose item master holds only code, user and date (the hypothesised bad-capture case), the coder cannot see a prior settlement, so Q5 cannot be answered 'yes' and cases fall to 5, 3 or 1, never 7. Gate 6 (more than 20% uncodable) will not fire because the tree does not produce 'uncodable'. Measured H is therefore a lower bound exactly where the product would matter, and the lower-of-two-coders pre-adjudication rule, which is a sound anti-drift measure, also discards the adjudicator's knowledge of unrecorded positions. The trade-off is real and unacknowledged; a per-case record-sufficiency score with H reported conditional on it is the minimum fix.

weakened.point: Pilot gate: kappa at least 0.70 on the eight-way primary code from 30 cases.
weakened.why: Thirty cases across eight categories with an expected H prevalence of 5 to 15% gives a kappa estimate with a standard error large enough (estimate: roughly 0.1 to 0.15) that the gate passes or fails by chance. Gate on the binary (7 or 8 versus other) with 50 to 60 pilot cases, and treat the eight-way kappa as descriptive.

weakened.point: Escalation stratum proxies (completedAt minus createdAt over one working day; modifiedUserId differs from createdUserId; needs-review status).
weakened.why: The Avalara fields exist as claimed (ItemHSCodeClassificationStatusModel: status, details, createdAt, completedAt, createdUserId, modifiedUserId; ClassificationCriteriaModel: TariffCodeNeedsReview; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avadev/AvaTax-REST-V2-DotNet-SDK/main/src/models/, vendor SDK source, fetched this session). But elapsed time is confounded by queue backlog, a second modifier is often data maintenance rather than review, and the needs-review flag is a vendor bulk-job criterion whose semantics are undocumented in the SDK. The design admits cross-company comparison is invalid under proxies but still sets a single 15% gate on 'the escalation stratum'. Also missing: if the company has fewer than roughly 100 identifiable escalations a year, the stratum cannot reach the stated n and H8 is already answered by volume; the design should say the experiment is not run in that case.

weakened.point: Interview questions are mostly neutral, but several presuppose or pitch.
weakened.why: Q12 ('If, at the moment of classifying a new item, a tool showed this question was settled on date X by Y for family Z, what would you do with it') is a hypothetical product pitch; stated intentions about a described tool are weak evidence (Yan 2026, 113 participants, 114 of 140 rules set to 'ask me' when pre-authoring policies, prior_evidence.md). Q5 ('Name three interpretive questions your team settled') presupposes that family-level settlements exist; Q4 ('how often do you re-decide anyway') and Q7's second half ('cases where you had already decided the question but it was applied differently') presuppose the failure mode. Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6, Q9, Q10, Q13 are well formed. Replace Q5 with 'tell me about the last time two people, or you and your broker, gave different codes to similar items', and drop Q12 or move it to the end as an explicit pitch whose answer is not scored.

Most would kill what they claim, but three are miscalibrated. 'Escalations are in the low hundreds a year' kills the importer path but not the broker pooled-queue path the design relies on (N over 10,000), so it is a partial kill unless the broker path is also dropped. The H1 kill is stated on delay ('most delay is spec sheets') while the addressable quantity is escalation share; H1 being true of delay is compatible with a non-trivial H among escalations, and the design's own stratum proxy (delay over one day) is dominated by missing facts by construction. 'Settled readings already sit in ONESOURCE, Descartes, SAP GTS or Avalara with approval and version history' can only be tested against Avalara's SDK; [RECALL, unverified] SAP GTS records change documents on classification objects, which would already give who and when. Missing kills: the importer has no internal classifier and the broker does it per line (then there is no importer buyer and the buyer is the broker, with the conflict noted above); and nobody at the company writes family-general positions at all (category 8 impossible by practice).

weakened.point: Wedge condition (i), 'the decision owner also holds rule-making power over the object being settled'.
weakened.why: Only partly. The trade compliance lead can set the company's risk position and instruct brokers, but the meaning of the heading is owned by CBP, HMRC or the EU, and a company position binds nobody else; the design concedes this in what_it_cannot_decide ('a company position is a risk stance, not a binding ruling'). Condition (i) is met for the company's own filings and not for the settled object. That is still better than mortgage or claims, as the design argues, but it should be stated as partial.

weakened.point: '114 of 5,193 six-digit lines account for half of all ruling line mentions' as evidence of coarse class recurrence.
weakened.why: Recomputed: 115 of 5,202 lines for half of 242,853 mentions over the whole corpus (same CSV, my parse), so the figure is right. But the concentration is inflated by chapter 99 additional-duty lines: in 2023-24, 9903.88 alone contributes 1,139 of 5,026 six-digit mentions (22.7%), and 44.3% of rulings mention more than one 6-digit line only because of those add-on lines (10.4% once chapters 98 and 99 are excluded). Excluding chapters 98 and 99, 85 lines cover half of 2023-24 mentions, not 37 (my recomputation). Recurrence at class level is still real, but the headline concentration should be quoted excluding chapter 98 and 99 lines. Also, 1,833 to 2,138 per year counts all rulings; rulings whose only category is Classification were 1,387 (2023) and 1,617 (2024).

weakened.point: 'The incumbent gap is documented, even if narrow.'
weakened.why: It is documented for one vendor only. Avalara's models were confirmed by fetch (TaxRuleModel has effectiveDate, endDate, description, no rationale; ItemPremiumClassificationOutputModel has a free-text 'justification' with createdUserId and createdDate; ClassificationModel.isPremium). ONESOURCE, Descartes, E2open, SAP GTS and Oracle GTM were unreachable (customs cluster, missing item 7). The design lists this as research gap 6 and then uses 'documented' in the wedge rationale; it should say 'documented at Avalara, unverified elsewhere'. The competitive-threat call is otherwise consistent with the digest: H6 is the best-supported hypothesis across clusters (ServiceNow exception, approval, decision-table and case-to-knowledge objects; Marble RuleSnooze and versioned ScenarioIteration; HMRC ATaR; PubLedge parked at 0 stars), and the digest's own position notes reach the same 'feature or service layer' conclusion.

weakened.point: Broker as a sample company for categories 7 and 8.
weakened.why: At a broker, the 'authorised person stating the reading in family-general terms' is the client, not the broker's classification manager, and a broker cannot ratify a position across clients. The protocol does not say who counts as the authority in broker records, so category 8 and gate 4 are undefined for the broker stratum.

strengthened.point: The CROSS statistics the design relies on.
strengthened.why: All recomputed from the same file this session (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justinmoonjeli/CROSSFetch/main/cbp_rulings_data.csv, open-source scrape of a government database, 216,164 rows): rulings per year 1,951 (2021), 1,848 (2022), 1,833 (2023), 2,138 (2024); HQ 201 to 215 a year in 2022-24; 20.9% cite a related ruling (23.4 to 23.8% in 2023-24); 1.41% ever modified or revoked; in 2023-24, 99.0% of rulings on a 6-digit line with a prior ruling and 89.1% on a 10-digit line with a prior ruling (98.3% and 87.4% by the first-tariff-only method the verifier used). The design's numbers are correct, and its reading of them (fresh human decision per product on settled lines, B/A dominance, public loop small) is the honest one.

strengthened.point: Structured export from Avalara is real.
strengthened.why: ItemModel (itemCode, description, itemGroup, category, createdDate, createdUserId, modifiedDate, modifiedUserId, source), ItemHSCodeClassificationStatusModel (country, status, details, createdAt, completedAt, createdUserId, modifiedUserId), ClassificationModel (productCode, systemCode, country, isPremium), ClassificationCriteriaModel (NoTariffCodeAssigned, InvalidTariffCode, TariffCodeNeedsReview) and ClassificationDetailsModel (classified, inProgress, notClassified, failed, notFound) all fetched from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avadev/AvaTax-REST-V2-DotNet-SDK/main/src/models/ (vendor SDK source). Where the sample company uses Avalara for HS classification the decision-packet fields exist; the caveat is that the share of mid-size importers that do so is unknown.

strengthened.point: HMRC Decision record as the settlement-record checklist.
strengthened.why: Decision.scala fetched (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmrc/binding-tariff-classification/main/app/uk/gov/hmrc/bindingtariffclassification/model/Decision.scala, government source code): bindingCommodityCode, effectiveStartDate, effectiveEndDate, justification, goodsDescription, methodSearch, methodCommercialDenomination, methodExclusion, appeal, cancellation, explanation. Using it as the packet checklist is sound. Bonus the design missed: RejectReason.scala (same repo) includes ATAR_RULING_ALREADY_EXISTS and DUPLICATE_APPLICATION, which is the regulator's own operational analogue of category 7 and gives the coders a worked definition of 'already settled, re-requested'.

strengthened.point: The wedge is chosen for access and says so.
strengthened.why: The design states the prior (single-digit to low-teens H), calls the executive evidence-against verdict evidence against itself, and names the workflow as the cheapest place to get an answer. That matches the digest: the customs verifier calls in-company classification 'the only candidate worth a base-rate experiment' and the independent position notes reach the same wedge for the same reason. The 'why not the larger markets' section is consistent with the banking, payments, claims and regulatory-reporting verifier verdicts in the digest (GSE-owned meaning, courts and FOS, EBA-run store, PSP in-house tooling, human-review mandates).

The binomial arithmetic is right (about plus or minus 3.5 points at n = 400 and 15%; about plus or minus 5 at n = 200). Fixing gates before coding, blinding coders to the hypothesis, and scoring on the lower coder's pre-adjudication share are the right defences against adjudication drift, subject to the thin-record trade-off noted above.

'No company will export a log within the sprint' and 'pilot cannot reach the kappa gate after one revision' are treated as results, not obstacles, and the go or no-go after interview six is a real checkpoint. That makes the sprint falsifiable, which most discovery plans are not.

strengthened.point: Category 7's 'found and applied is coded 1' rule.
strengthened.why: Correct in principle: the working state the product claims to create is a settled reading applied without re-decision, so it must not be counted as H. The rule only needs to be reconciled with gate 3 (see refuted).

missing: A zero-coder inconsistency metric computed from the item master before any coding: items in the same itemGroup or with near-identical descriptions carrying different codes for the same country; the same item carrying different codes across group entities or brokers; items whose code was changed after a post-entry correction. This gives a first signal of capture failure at no coding cost and is the natural replacement for the vacuous gate 3.

A short prospective shadow test (four to eight weeks) in which each new escalation is checked against the list of settlements captured from the retrospective sample, counting hits and whether the specialist would have applied the settlement. The design says retrospective coding cannot show retrieval at the moment of decision; this is the cheap way to get a first reading.

A per-case record-sufficiency score (which of the Decision.scala elements the company record holds) pre-registered as a secondary outcome, with the H share reported conditional on it and a stated interpretation: if most settlements carry no rationale field, that supports the capture gap and simultaneously means category 7 is undercounted in this sample.

A computable definition of the recurrence class for gate 2: the interpretive class assigned only to coded cases, with recurrence measured as coded cases per class within a 24-month window (12 months for sampling, a further 12 for recurrence to avoid censoring), and line-or-family recurrence reported separately and labelled factual recurrence.
The authority rule for broker records (who counts as the authorised person for category 8 and gate 4) and the consent path for importer data held by a broker, plus the broker's per-line fee conflict.

Year-one payback that counts category 8 at its expected within-year reuse rather than at r, subtracts capture and backfill cost, and states the central-case gate (36% at the design's own estimates) next to the tail-case 15%.
A minimum stratum size (estimate: about 100 identifiable escalations a year) below which the experiment is not run because H8 is already answered by volume at that company.

Per-case recording of the duty-rate differential between the candidate codes, so that a risk-avoided or duty-savings case can be computed later even though the design rightly excludes it from the labour payback at sale.
Separation of interviewer and coder roles, so that the coders are blind not only to the hypothesis but to what interviewees said about recurrence.

Moving the GTM-vendor interview earlier, or adding a documentation check on SAP GTS change documents and ONESOURCE approval workflows, so that the H6 question (fields already exist) is answered before coding rather than after.

A pre-registered secondary analysis using HMRC's ATAR_RULING_ALREADY_EXISTS and DUPLICATE_APPLICATION reject reasons as the coding analogue for category 7, and, for the UK or EU importer, the public ATaR search as the precedent lookup (gov.uk was blocked this session; the site is public).

A named fallback if no customs company exports a log: the digest's other uncertain pockets (KYC/CDD exception logs, PSP merchant-onboarding queues) with the same protocol, so that the sprint's stop result is 'untestable here' rather than 'untestable'.
corrected_verdict: The wedge choice stands: in-company customs classification is the only workflow the digest leaves as uncertain rather than negative, it is chosen for access and says so, and the design's public-corpus numbers survive recomputation. The competitive-threat call ('feature inside an existing workflow product', with a broker or advisory service layer second and 'not built' as the live outcome) is consistent with the digest's incumbent evidence (H6 best supported; Avalara, ServiceNow, Marble, HMRC) and stands, with the caveat that the incumbent gap is documented only at Avalara. The discovery sprint is usable after removing the product-pitch question, rephrasing the three presupposing questions, adding the broker consent and conflict handling, and adding the two missing kills (no internal classifier; no family positions in practice). The base-rate experiment is not runnable as written and must be repaired before pre-registration: gate 3 is vacuous under the category 7 definition, gate 2 is not computable because unsampled items cannot be assigned an interpretive class, gate 5 fails by construction at the 10-digit line and its lookup source has no ruling text, the non-specialist coder cannot execute the decision tree so a kappa failure would be uninformative, and the written gate 1 (15%) is the tail-scenario value while the design's own central economics require 36%. With those repairs the experiment is worth running at one willing company, and the honest prior remains that it returns categories 7 plus 8 below the gate, which would confirm the digest's executive call (evidence against a standalone product) and leave a feature request to the item-master vendor or a service line for a broker as the residual. Evidence limitation: no volume, cost, price or escalation figure for this workflow was sourced by anyone in the project; every such number is an estimate or recall and the gates must be filled from interviews before coding.
overall:
Evidence limitation first: the session's search quota was exhausted and every regulator, vendor, association and press host was blocked, so this review verified only what GitHub serves. I re-fetched and parsed the CROSSFetch CSV (216,164 rulings) and reproduced the design's figures: 1,833 to 2,138 rulings a year in 2023-24, 20.9% citing a related ruling, 1.41% ever modified or revoked, 99.0% of 2023-24 rulings on a previously ruled 6-digit line and 89.1% on a previously ruled 10-digit line, 115 of 5,202 six-digit lines covering half of all line mentions. I also confirmed the Avalara SDK fields (item status with completedAt and user stamps, TariffCodeNeedsReview, premium free-text justification, no rationale on TaxRule) and the HMRC Decision record. The structural case for the wedge is therefore as good as the design says, and no better: the public loop is small and re-decides per product on settled lines, so the prior for in-company H is single digits to low teens (customs verifier), and the design says so.

The design's weaknesses are in the experiment, not the wedge. Four of six gates are mis-specified: gate 3 always passes because category 7 is defined as re-decided cases only; gate 2 needs interpretive classes for unsampled items that nobody has coded; gate 5 fails by construction because nearly every US decision sits on an already-ruled line and the named lookup file has no ruling text; gate 1's 15% is the favourable tail of the design's own model, whose central case requires 36%, above every H estimate in the project. The two-coder plan fails on its own terms because the tree requires reading the tariff and coder B cannot, so the kappa gate would measure coder competence, not category separability. The protocol also systematically under-counts category 7 in companies with thin records, which is the population the product targets, and the anti-drift rule (lower coder, pre-adjudication) makes that worse without acknowledging the trade-off. The concentration statistic is inflated by chapter 99 additional-duty lines (9903.88 is 22.7% of 2023-24 six-digit mentions); excluding chapters 98 and 99, 85 lines cover half of 2023-24 mentions, not 37.

The sprint is better than most: neutral opening questions, real stop conditions, a go or no-go after interview six. It needs the pitch question removed, three presupposing questions rephrased, the broker consent and fee-conflict problem handled ([RECALL, unverified] broker client records need importer consent under 19 CFR 111.24), and kills added for 'no internal classifier' and 'no family positions in practice'. The competitive-threat call matches the digest across clusters and should stand, worded as 'documented at Avalara, unverified at ONESOURCE, Descartes, SAP GTS and Oracle GTM'.

Corrected verdict: keep the wedge and the feature call; repair the experiment (gates 1, 2, 3 and 5, coder qualifications, record-sufficiency reporting, a zero-coder inconsistency metric from the item master, and a short prospective shadow test) before pre-registering; run it at one willing company; expect it to return H below the economic gate and to confirm the project's executive call of evidence against a standalone product.
